newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco puts bought, calls sold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco puts bought, calls sold.

text.p: Investors were busy buying Cisco Systems Inc puts and selling calls as the stock dropped in heavy action, traders said Tuesday.
By 1435 CST/2035 GMT, Cisco was off 2-1/4 at 56-3/4 on volume of more than 26.8 million shares.
The networking equipment maker's chief executive officer said at a technology conference in San Francisco that backlog of sales was getting smaller and that international sales growth was slowing.
"We had a lot of put buyers coming in when the news initially came out," Patrick Hamilton at LETCO said.
"Then a lot of call sellers too," he said. "People were just looking to get short stock."
Cisco shares reached a session low of 55-1/4 before recovering.
"There is some technical damage" to the stock's chart, said Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, referring to the selloff.
He noted that the stock has broken below its February 10 low at 58 as well as its 200-day and 50-day moving averages.
The stock peaking at 75-3/4 intraday on January 21, when it closed at 74-7/8.
"It's joining the list of sloppy-looking charts that includes U.S. Robotics, Intel and IBM (International Business Machines), which still looks sloppy," Nie said. "That list is lengthening a bit."
U.S. Robotics was up 2-3/8 at 61-1/2 Tuesday, Intel gained 1/4 at 149-1/4 and IBM added 3-1/4 at 147.
All three stocks are attempting to recover from recent sharp selloffs.
But Cisco's chart pattern is not outright bearish, and support should emerge in an old support zone in the 52 area, Nie said.
LETCO's Hamilton said the stock and the options settled in to relatively calm trading after early decline, although volume remained strong.
By late afternoon, the Cisco March 60 calls were most active in the group, with total volume of about 6,720 contracts. The March 50 put traded a total of about 6,100.
Hamilton said most of the put buying was centered in the March 55 and 60s.
The March 55 put traded a total of 3,826 contracts and the March 60 put traded 3,675.
Cisco options trade at the CBOE and the AMEX.
Despite the concentration of activity in the Cisco March options, activity was solid in the April, July and October series also.
The July 55 put traded a total of 3,705 contracts and the July 65 call traded more than 2,900.
Hamilton said volatilities in the options rose about four points off the early drop in the stock but retreated slightly after that.
